results.content:
Maher El Ouahabi    · Updated   · 11 min read

Brand Radar is Ahrefs’ AI visibility product, and it measures something no other tool in this comparison does: Reddit, YouTube and TikTok alongside the AI engines. That matters more than it sounds, because when we asked Google’s AI which GEO tool to use, Reddit and YouTube were cited in every single run and every funded vendor was cited in none.

It is also not a plan. It is an add-on on top of an Ahrefs subscription, and the number most reviews quote is not the number you will pay.

> Disclosure: EchoWi competes with Ahrefs on AI visibility. Prices and platform lists below were read from Ahrefs’ own pages on 6 August 2026.

## The short version [...] Brand Radar AI, the part that tracks AI answers, is a separate add-on that Ahrefs lists from €179 a month, with an all-platforms tier shown at £560 a month on the product page.

So the real arithmetic is a base plan plus the add-on:

| Ahrefs plan | Plan price | With Brand Radar AI |
 --- 
| Starter | €27 | €206 |
| Lite | €119 | €298 |
| Standard | €229 | €408 |
| Advanced | €419 | €598 |

Read from Ahrefs’ pricing page and the Brand Radar product page on 6 August 2026.

Put that beside the rest of the market and the position is clear. Rankscale is €20 for ten engines, Otterly is $29, Profound and Semrush are both $99. Brand Radar’s realistic entry is somewhere between €206 and €408 depending on which Ahrefs plan you need for everything else. [...] Skip to content

TL;DR

Finding the best Ahrefs alternatives in 2026 comes down to three things: whether the tool tracks where you appear in AI answers (not just Google rankings), whether the data is fresh enough for your actual workflow, and whether it produces actions or just reports. Our number one pick is Omnia for founders and lean marketing teams at VC-backed startups who need GEO execution, not just a dashboard to check occasionally.

Ahrefs built one of the best SEO tools of the last decade. The problem in 2026 is that a growing share of your buyers never see a search results page at all. They ask ChatGPT, get an answer, and move on. Ahrefs wasn't built for that world, and no amount of add-on pricing changes the architecture underneath it.
